hints: Look at where label 1 sits in this anterior view. It is the large vessel coming out of the front of the heart, in front of the big arch behind it.

Remember the rule for valve position. Atrioventricular valves sit between atrium and ventricle with tendinous cords, while semilunar valves sit at the base of the two great arteries leaving the ventricles.
walkthrough:
**Get your orientation right**

This is an anterior (front) view, so the right side of the heart appears on the left side of the diagram. The right side receives deoxygenated blood and pumps it to the lungs.

Think: right atrium and right ventricle are on the left of the picture.

**Identify the great vessels, labels 1 and 4**

Label 1 is the vessel leaving the front ventricle (the right ventricle) and dividing toward the lungs. That is the pulmonary artery, not the aorta which arches behind it.

Label 4 is a vessel entering the right atrium from above. That is the vena cava (superior vena cava) bringing blood back from the body.

**Identify the two valves, labels 2 and 3**

Label 2 is at the base of the great artery leaving a ventricle, with no cords attached. That is the position of a semilunar valve.

Label 3 is between the atrium and ventricle on the right side, with thin cords (chordae tendineae) anchoring the flaps. That is the position of an atrioventricular valve (the tricuspid valve).

**Match to the table**

So we have: 1 = pulmonary artery, 2 = semilunar valve, 3 = atrioventricular valve, 4 = vena cava. That matches row C exactly.

options.A: Incorrect because 1 is not the aorta. The aorta is the arch behind, while 1 is the pulmonary artery in front.
options.B: Incorrect because 1 and 4 are not pulmonary veins. Pulmonary veins enter the left atrium at the back, not these front vessels.
options.C: Correct. 1 is the pulmonary artery, 2 is the semilunar valve, 3 is the atrioventricular valve with cords, and 4 is the vena cava.
options.D: Incorrect because it swaps the valves. Label 2 is the semilunar valve and label 3 is the atrioventricular valve, not the other way round.
